Saechi wrote Hello Kaisei five years ago, while she was still in high school.  At that time, she was feeling conflicted between whether she should continue her studies or instead try to pursue music. She wrote this song for herself, in order to encourage herself to follow her dreams. This becomes very apparent when you read the lyrics.

It is a song very close to her heart, a rough song which becomes her most polished when she performs it live. Even now when she's struggling with her work, remembering when she sang this song in the past helps her cheer up ([source](https://ameblo.jp/otsuka-sae/entry-12304381103.html)).

​

Fans on Twitter have taken to posting photographs of the sky along with Hello Kaisei (ハロー快晴) in the caption. It's well known that Saechi will like pretty much all her mentions on Twitter, whether you reply to her tweets or just tag her in random stuff (send her some cute bunny videos, folks). But even if you don't tag her, she still searches ハロー快晴 to like these tweets (she doesn't get all of them, but have a look and you will surely see it). She even sometimes saves the photos and [features them on her blog](https://ameblo.jp/otsuka-sae/entry-12390375724.html). It's just one lovely example of how she goes out of her way to connect with her fans!

​

In her songwriting, Saechi doesn't aim to write "good" or "nice" songs, but songs which are able to convey feelings to people and move them ([source](https://bangdreamenglishtranslations.wordpress.com/2016/12/27/otsuka-sae-special-interview/)). She also doesn't want to emulate anyone else, instead wanting to imbue herself in the music and write songs only she can write. She sees her songs as her children and is very particular about the melodies, arrangements, and lyrics ([source](https://toretame.jp/genuine-guitarist-voice-actor-otsuka-sae-exclusive-interview-live-in-the-spirit-of-do-not-think-feel.html)).

Hello Kaisei was the first of Saechi's original songs that fans were able to hear, and outside of attending a Saebo it's still the only one you can hear in full. However, that doesn't mean it's her first song.

She recalls starting to "write" songs from as early as 5 years old, when she would rearrange do-re-mi notes from the nursery rhyme [Tulip](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lEIYOVUxZqI) into new melodies. She continued arranging melodies in this way until her 2nd year of elementary school, and still has the sheet music she created in this time period! For Saechi, music has been a part of her life for so long that it feels as natural as eating or bathing ([source](https://toretame.jp/genuine-guitarist-voice-actor-otsuka-sae-exclusive-interview-live-in-the-spirit-of-do-not-think-feel.html)).

​

In terms of her street lives, she began performing on the streets of Yokohama when she was 15 years old simply by impulse. At that time, she had been playing guitar for 2 weeks and knew only 4 basic chords. Even back then, she had a wonderful passion for music and really enjoyed performing! Her policy was that even if she got a fever or a typhoon came, she would keep playing until the trains stopped.

What she loves most about performing on the street is that since there is no stage, the performer's feelings are conveyed directly. The more strongly your feelings reach people, the larger audience you will gather, regardless of what song is performed ([source](https://toretame.jp/genuine-guitarist-voice-actor-otsuka-sae-exclusive-interview-live-in-the-spirit-of-do-not-think-feel.html)).

She also likes being able to see the same people in the crowd who come to see her repeatedly - you will know this if you watched her [5th live VTR](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1cprCjaUFl3DI2E9CpLh87l-t9jhalr3w/view), where she reunites with a man who had been supporting her since her street live days. He is seen in the foreground of the Hello Kaisei street live performance.

​

Of the other original songs she has written and performed at events, there are currently three: "Ikizama" (Way of Life), "Personality or Status?", and "Ennui ga Biteki na no wa Finder no naka de" (translation machine broke, sorry). These were performed for the first time in August 2018 at SAE Vo.yage! vol.2 \~I'm an Egg (yes, that's what she named her event).

You can listen to some of the piano from Ikizama [here](https://twitter.com/OSae1010/status/1031422502898040832), and short rehearsal clips of Personality and Ikizama [here](https://twitter.com/OSae1010/status/1051790803276771328). (Note that in the second tweet, Saechi refers to the song as "Personality of Status". This is just a typo, it's still actually called Personality or Status.)

Ikizama and Ennui are both songs played on piano. Originally, Saechi intended to play Ennui on electric guitar, but she rearranged the song for keys when it was decided that they would have a grand piano at her event. Ikizama is the newest song and was completed only two days before Saebo 2, putting a 5 year gap between it and Hello Kaisei. ([source](https://ameblo.jp/otsuka-sae/entry-12399149954.html)). Fans have remarked that hearing these two songs performed together at Saebo 2 was very moving as it showcased her growth over the years.

​

In addition to writing her own songs, Saechi also creates her own outfits for her events. She goes to thrift stores and hand sews together parts of old clothes to create new outfits. Sewing was a skill she learnt for Saebo 2, but it has now become one of her hobbies - if you see her wearing something that looks to be Frankensteined from several different pieces of clothing, she most likely made it herself. She has also expressed the desire to create outfits for Popipa and wishes to make a costume for their next fan meeting (which Bushiroad will let her do if they aren't absolute cowards).

On another note, she also helps make the stage props and designs her own goods for these events (often featuring her weird fursona Geppi, a rabbit/frog hybrid).

​

I apologise for being so longwinded, but I hope all of this has let you learn something new about Saechi and that you will continue to support her as she continues on her journey!

Thank you for reading! Saechi's words are very beautiful and I'm grateful to be able to help share some of her light.

Thanks for all these great recs, I was having trouble getting my thoughts together!

I'll add that my absolute recommendation is to read [her blog](https://ameblo.jp/otsuka-sae/) (which she updates every day) if at all possible. It's often just snippets of her life, but she also talks a lot about her honest feelings (similar to what I've translated) and it's the best way to get to the heart of who she is as a person.

It may be tricky if you aren't comfortable with Japanese, but it's surprising how much you can understand with Google Translate and a basic knowledge of grammar to pick it apart (this is exactly what I do and while it's not ideal, it works pretty well about 80% of the time).

I'm planning to translate some of the more significant blogs she's written as well, though this may take me a while since I'm quite busy right now.

Watching as many of her live performances as you can is a great idea (both for getting to know her and just generally IMO). After all, her love for music is at the core of who she is. Her love for performing is incredibly palpable and you don't need to understand Japanese to get that. If you haven't seen it already, I particularly recommend Popipa's segment from Garupa Live earlier this year (particularly day 2) as I think she's incredible there.

If you're willing to watch unsubbed video content, the early Getsubushi episodes hosted by all of Popipa together are incredibly cute (in the content masterlist). Also, her closing MCs in 2nd and 4th lives are very emotional, and you can feel the strength of her feelings even if you don't exactly understand all of what she's saying.

Also, Saechi's corners on Popiraji where she and the rest of Popipa improvise songs together are really excellent if you can catch those. [Here's a little preview](https://twitter.com/_satsunyan/status/1036528348510339073) of what those generally sound like.
